newsitem.title: GERMANY: Higher German oilseeds area seen in 1997-ministry.
newsitem.headline: Higher German oilseeds area seen in 1997-ministry.

text.p: Germany's oilseeds acreage for both food and industrial uses may be expanded to just over one million hectares, 15 percent above last year's figure, the farm ministry said in a weekly circular.
It cited farmers' replies to an official survey.
Rapeseed was put at roughly one million ha -- consisting of 457,000 ha in western Germany (412,000 ha in 1996) and 543,000 ha in eastern Germany (442,000 previously).
The 1997 sunseed area was pegged at 30,000 ha (44,000 ha).
Out of the rapeseed total, winter plantings alone were put at 956,000 ha, 23 percent more than a year earlier.
Germany may plant a total 836,099 ha to winter and spring oilseeds for food use under the bilateral U.S./European Blair House accord.
Farmers must pay penalties if they overshoot the area.
The ministry said it was unclear whether total plantings for food use would fall short of the Blair House limit or exceed it, and only final data would be conclusive.

Results of a private survey from the Union for the Promotion of Oil and Protein Crops (Ufop) earlier this month said farmers intended to restrict the 1997 oilseeds acreage for food use to 741,000 ha, well below the Blair House limit.

Traders said an increase in oilseeds sowings for the 1997 harvest had been expected because of a lower land set-aside rate and because rapeseed prices were high after one third of the 1996 crop had been lost to winter damage.
